threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think you can catch a tube home late on a strike night. Everyone else is walking, but you’re out here waiting for a bus that’ll never come.
Last night on the 59, a guy spilled his drink and tried to mop it up with a burger wrapper. Didn't even blink when the driver shouted at him.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw the kids playing football in the street, while the café next door served espresso to their parents. Just another Saturday afternoon.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a converted factory that serves homemade cakes alongside rotating art exhibits. It's a slice of local creativity.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local when they instinctively know to dodge the BART delays but still complain about the 14 bus being late.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today with a guy playing a saxophone in the back. The driver didn’t even bat an eye—just another Tuesday in the TL.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the plazas, but the best vibes are in the narrow streets where locals actually live and hang out.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they stand at the metro entrance, staring at the map like it’s a lost treasure map.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: Trying to pay for your latte with a card and not knowing you might as well be offering gold dust here in Dalston.
Last night on the 196, a guy serenaded the entire bus with opera. Even the drunks stopped arguing to listen—surreal Brixton moment.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a kid selling homemade lemonade on the corner, and the customers were all adults happily paying €2. That’s Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you stumble upon a street party that turns a quiet courtyard into a vibrant art gallery, complete with local DJs and eclectic food stalls.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they can spot a BART train delay by the way the crowd shuffles at 16th St. Station.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a chicken costume trying to board the 38. Muni driver shook his head and the dude just waved. Only in San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals are sipping wine at plaza del Sol, but most of us are just trying to escape the crowds and enjoy a quiet moment at home.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by their baffled expressions at the slow pace of the metro during rush hour, still expecting it to run like clockwork.
